https://metro.co.uk/galleries/34-must-wa.title: 34 must-watch films with a 100% on Rotten Tomatoes – and where to find them

image.caption: Looking for something good to watch tonight? You could pick up a recent blockbuster, or an Oscar winning movie you've heard great things about. But what if you fancied a film which, according to the critics, was perfect? Even the big award-winners don't always score critical acclaim across the board - so instead, why not turn to Rotten Tomatoes' coveted list of films with a 100% rating to find your next watch? Only a handful of movies have been handed that accolade, the perfect score which means that they haven't had a single bad review from any critic, anywhere. And while many of those who get the big hundred tend to be smaller, obscure movies which won't have been playing at your local Odeon, there are some stone cold classics and box office winners in there too. So, if you want to see what a 100% rated film actually looks like, consider popping on one of these tonight. You may not have heard of all of them, they may not all star A-listers, but every one of them is brilliant...(Picture: Netflix)

Kicking off our rundown is this little drama which hopped under the radar in 2018 but wowed all those who saw it - largely due to the impressive film debut of Last Night In Soho star Thomasin Harcourt McKenzie. Leave No Trace sees McKenzie and US actor Ben Foster as a father and daughter living a perfect but mysterious existence in a Portland nature reserve - until a small mistake tips them off to the authorities, sending them off on an erratic journey to find a new home. Directed by Debra Granik - who previously directed Jennifer Lawrence to her first Oscar nomination in Winter's Bone - the critics couldn't find a bad thing to say about this one. The Mail On Sunday said of the film: 'It's both thought-provoking and life-affirming,' while Rolling Stone called it 'hypnotic, haunting and one of the year's best'Where to watch it: Leave No Trace is available on Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+  and Google Play (Picture: Allstar/UNIVERSAL PICTURES)

It's unusual to find a sequel that improves on its predecessor, with only a handful of movies achieveing that feat, but Toy Story 2 is widely regarded as one of those movies. The follow-up to the groundbreaking 1995 smash Toy Story, this sees Woody (Tom Hanks) and Buzz (Tim Allen) returning to the playroom, in a movie which sees Woody kidnapped by a toy collector. However, after he's unexpectedly reunited with old friends including cowgirl doll Jessie (Joan Cusack) and sidekick Stinky Pete The Prospector (Kelsey Grammar), getting him back to Andy's is going to prove quite the challenge for the others. Critics praised the film for being just as original and inventive as the first in the series - if not more. 'Toy Story 2 is a brilliant example of that rarest of Hollywood phenomena - a sequel to a major hit film that's as good, if not better, than the original,' CNN said in their reviewWhere to watch it: Toy Story 2 is available on on Disney Plus, Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+ and Google Play(Picture: Allstar/PIXAR/DISNEY)

The first documentary on this list comes to us from this year's Sundance Film Festival, where it won the Audience Award earlier this year before being picked up by Netflix. Daughters centres on four incarcerated men and their daughters. Specifically it follows the four girls as they prepare for a special Daddy Daughter dance event - which forms part of a unique program in prisons in Washington DC. IndieWire wrote: 'An enormously moving documentary made all the more effective by co-directors Angela Patton and Natalie Rae’s steadfast refusal to settle for easy sentiment in the face of difficult outcomes.' Viewers also had a strong reaction to this one, with many saying it had them sobbing throughout. One said on X: ‘Bruh who let me watch Daughters on Netflix. I was not prepared to cry like this,'  while Ciarra another added: 'This should be required viewing upon entry for men with daughters. Ain’t no way you can’t understand the pain you’re causing your children after watching this.’Where to watch it: Daughters is available to watch on Netflix(Picture: Getty Images)

One for fans of 80s music - specifically New Wave legends Talking Heads - Stop Making Sense is an exhilarating music documentary which captures the band live onstage across four nights of their 1983 tour. Expect to hear - and see - such classic tracks as Psycho Killer, Burning Down The House, This Must Be The Place and Once In A Lifetime, as well as Girlfriend Is Better - from whose lyrics the film gets its title. Directed by Jonathan Demme, who later went on to win an Oscar for The Silence Of The Lambs, it's widely regarded by critics as one of the greatest concert films of all time, with The Guardian saying: 'The pleasure of the music is overpowering,' while the New Yorker added: 'In its own terms Stop Making Sense is close to perfection'Where to watch it: Stop Making Sense is available on Amazon Prime Video, and Apple TV Plus(Picture: Everett/REX/Shutterstock)

If you're in the mood for a chilling evening's viewing then you should add this creepy shocker to your watchlist immediately - more so given that it wowed critics when it first dropped in 2020. His House focuses on a refugee couple from South Sudan, who are granted probational asylum in the UK after fleeing their war-torn homeland and given a house on the outskirts of London complete with strict restrictions to avoid deportation. However the pair struggle to adjust to their new life - even more so when it becomes apparent that evil is lurking beneath the surface of their new home. With a cast that includes Wunmi Mosaku (Luther, Loki) and former Dr Who Matt Smith, critics loved the fact that the film goes way beyond standard horror tropes to explore deeper themes. 'His House is a Netflix horror film that goes beyond supernatural scares, exploring themes of grief, guilt, and the struggle to belong,' Collider wrote.Where to watch it: His House is available to watch on Netflix and BBC iPlayer(Picture: Netflix/Moviestore/REX/Shutterstock)

It's no surprise to see several classic musicals from Hollywood's Golden Age getting the 100% treatment with this stone-cold classic featuring a post-Wizard Of Oz Judy Garland among them. Set in 1904 on the cusp of Christmas, it sees Garland take the lead as one of four upper-middle-class sisters negotiating life and love in the titular city - and having to come to terms with leaving it all behind for a new life in New York. It's all very feelgood and rather wonderful, and of course if you like big production numbers you'll be well served. Don't believe us? Then take it from the New York Daily News who said the film is 'a miracle of delightful entertainment that is a sure cure for the blues.'Where to watch it: Meet Me In St Louis is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+ and Google Play(Picture: Allstar/MGM)

Sticking with the theme of old classics, we have this 1944 film noir, about a Manhattan detective (Dana Andrews) who is investigating the murder of the title character (Gene Tierney), an art executive who was killed in her apartment on Madison Avenue. As he delves deeper into what happened, quizzing the dead woman's best friend and fiance as well as a notorious gossip columnist, he becomes more and more obsessed with the case - ultimately falling in love with her. There's barely a thing wrong with this movie as far as the critics are concerned. 80 years on it's still loved, with Empire Magazine saying: 'A classic noir romance where all of the cinematic elements fit together perfectly' and Little White Lies calling it 'one of the great noirs.'Where to watch it: Laura is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+ and Google Play

Serving as a reminder that animation isn't always cute and feelgood, Grave Of The Firelies is a truly powerful watch, following the story of orphans Seita and Setsuko and their struggle to survive during the final months of World War II. Widely regarded as a masterpiece of Japanese animation as well as one of the greatest war films ever made, it's one of those films you admire rather than enjoy - but while it may be one you can only bring yourself to watch once the reviews suggest you definitely should. One of the most startling and moving animated films ever,' said the New York Times while the Guardian agreed, saying: 'There are magical moments of natural beauty and childish delight, too - which only make the tragedy even more harrowing.'Where to watch it: Grave Of The Fireflies is available to watch on Netflix.(Picture: Studio Ghibli/Kobal/REX/Shutterstock)

We're heading back almost 100 years for this next one - to the days when films hadn't even discovered sound - but don't let any of this put you off, because Charlie Chaplin's The Gold Rush still ranks among one of the best films of all time. The iconic comic plays the Little Tramp, who heads north to join in the Klondike Gold Rush, but instead finds himself trapped in a snowed-in cabin with a successful prospector and a fugitive. When he eventually gets out it becomes apparent his fortunes could be about to change. Again it's kept the critics very happy, with Vanity Fair summing it up: 'The Gold Rush is Chaplin's greatest picture'.Where to watch it: The Gold Rush is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video and Plex(Picture: History Archive/REX/Shutterstock)

Another documentary film you won't want to miss, 2020's Crip Camp goes back to the 1970s to tell the story of a summer camp in New York for teens with disabilities - and how many of the campers went on to become activists in the disability rights movement. Critics had a lot of good things to say about this one, including the Financial Times, whose review read: 'How strange - and how telling - that despite the wealth of big-screen documentaries released in the past 20 years, the story behind the remarkable Crip Camp has so long gone untold'.Where to watch it: Crip Camp is available to watch on Netflix(Picture: Patti Smolian)

The final movie in a trilogy by Kyzystof Kieslowski based on the colours of the French flag, Red is widely regarded as the best in the series by miles - cementing its status as one of the best films of the 1990s. Irene Jacob stars as a model who accidentally runs over a dog belonging to a retired judge (Jean-Louis Trintignant), sparking off a chain of events which lead them to form an unexpected bond. The Radio Times were among the many critics who raved about this one, saying: 'The film's use of colour and sound is unparalleled in 1990s cinema, while the intricate plot linking model Jacob with snooping judge Jean-Louis Trintignant is spellbinding'.Where to watch it: Three Colours: Red is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV+(Picture: Film Four)

If you're in the mood for some comedy rather than an actual movie, then this 2018 Netflix special should hit the spot. Australian comedian Hannah Gadsby takes centre stage here, delivering a show which reshapes standard stand-up by pairing punchlines with personal revelations about gender, sexuality and childhood turmoil. Critics loved the comic's way of turning humour on its head, with Mashable saying: 'The beauty of this piece is found in its verbalization of what so many of us self-deprecators, professional and amateur alike, feel on a daily basis-a need to excuse our own existence'.Where to watch it: Hannah Gadsby: Nanette is available to watch on Netflix

This one comes fresh from the Sundance Film Festival, where it picked up the Grand Jury prize for directing. Sugarcane follows an investigation into the Canadian Indian residential school system, a network of boarding schools for indigenous peoples which subjected many students to physical and sexual abuse, as well as forcing them to live in inhuman conditions and depriving them of their legal identities. Screen International called it 'an accomplished, devastating documentary' while the Hollywood Reporter said it 'sensitively approaches a painful history'.Where to watch it: Sugarcane is still showing in selected cinemas, and will be released on Disney Plus, although the release date has yet to be confirmed(Picture: National Geographic)

The Terminator might have turned into a blockbuster franchise now, but back in 1984 the original film, starring Arnold Schwarzenegger, was a pretty low-budget affair - albeit one which went on to be a box office smash and spawn the far bigger budget Terminator 2: Judgment Day in 1991. The Austrian actor unites with James Cameron for the flick, in which he plays an unstoppable cyborg sent back in time to kill Sarah Connor (Linda Hamilton), a woman whose unborn son will one day save mankind from extinction by Skynet, a hostile artificial intelligence which exists in the future. Not only does it offer brilliant edge-of-the-seat Friday night thrills but it has a 100% Rotten Tomatoes rating too, with Time Out calling it 'damn close to perfect'. We agree.Where to watch it: The Terminator is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+ and Google Play(Picture: Channel 5)

As annoying as it  might be to use the word 'heartwarming' to describe a film, that really is the case for this hidden British gem, from the people who brought you the cult 1981 comedy Gregory's Girl. Peter Riegert takes the lead as a Texas oil executive who gets more than he bargained for when his boss (the legendary Burt Lancaster) sends him to a tiny Scottish village the company wants to buy out for a new refinery. But after spending time there, among the locals, his outlook on life changes - and he begins to wonder whether he's doing the right thing. The Times called this one 'a Scottish-American charmer with a sublime soundtrack' and they're spot on.Where to watch it: Local Hero is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV+(Picture: Enigma/Goldcrest/Kobal/REX/Shutterstock)

Just as Toy Story 2 has nabbed the coveted 100% rating, so indeed has its predecessor. The computer animated comedy burst on to screens in 1995 and was an instant hit as much for its groundbreaking visuals as for its engaging and hugely original story. Set in a nursery where toys come to life when the humans aren't looking, Tom Hanks plays cowboy doll Woody, whose position as his owner Andy's favourite toy comes under threat when space ranger Buzz Lightyear (Tim Allen) appears on the scene. Except the newcomer is convinced he is actually a real spaceman on a mission - leading to all manner of trouble which could end in the pair of them becoming lost toys. Quite simply, it's wonderful, and the critics agree. 'The year's most inventive comedy,' Time Magazine said while the Chicago Sun-Times' Rogert Ebert added: 'The result is a visionary roller-coaster ride of a movie'.Where to watch it: Toy Story is available to watch on Disney Plus, Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV+(Picture: Snap/REX/ Shutterstock)

Bees might have had their place in cinema (from Bee Movie to that infamous moment in 2006's The Wicker Man) but they get to take centre stage in this charming documentary from North Macedonia. Honeyland follows Haitzde, a beekeeping woman in a remote mountain village, whose old-school, traditional methods of bee cultivation come under threat from a neighbouring family. Filmed over three years, with more than 400 hours of footage shot to make the finished movie, it might not sound like action packed Saturday night entertainment but trust us, it'll draw you in. Reviews were stellar across the board, with the Scotsman summing it up: 'The end result is a subtly rendered story for our times'. Where to watch it: Honeyland is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+ and Google Play (Picture: Neon)

There's not a lot of romcoms nabbing a coveted spot on the 100% list, but this one - a proper Golden Age of Hollywood classic featuring the likes of Katharine Hepburn and Cary Grant - has unsurprisingly made it. Hepburn stars as Tracy Lord, a Philadelphia socialite who has split from her husband C.K Dexter Haven (Grant) due to his drinking and her overbearing nature. However, as she prepares for her wedding to husband number two, George Kittridge (John Howard), she has an encounter with her ex, and a prying reporter, Macaulay 'Mike' Connor (James Stewart), and is forced to confront her feelings for all three men. The film was a box office smash and won two Oscars - including a best actor prize for Stewart - and of course the critics adored it. 'I haven't enjoyed a film so much in years,' said the Daily Telegraph Australia. 'It is light, sophisticated comedy -- and how sophisticated!'Where to watch it: The Philadelphia Story is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+ and Google Play(Picture: SNAP/REX/Shutterstock)

The story of Pinocchio, the little wooden puppet who wants to be a real boy, has been made on several occasions but the original cartoon adaptation from the Walt Disney stable is the definitive version. Loosely based on the novel by Italian author Carlo Collodi, you'll know the story, you'll probably even know the songs (When You Wish Upon A Star, anyone?) But if you've never seen the actual movie, it's definitely one to add to your list, as it's widely regarded as one of the Mouse Kingdom's best ever. 'Taken as a whole, the picture is a masterpiece which sets another milestone along the road of screen entertainment,' the Hollywood Reporter said in its review, while the New York Daily News called it 'the most enchanting film ever brought to the screen.'Where to watch it: Pinocchio is available to watch on Disney Plus, Apple TV+ and Google Play(Picture: Disney)

Here's one which may be familiar to fans of the My Heart Will Go On singer, since it's notched up some great reviews and decent viewing figures since it dropped on to Amazon Prime in June. The documentary takes a no-holds-barred look at Celine's struggle against stiff person syndrome - and how the condition has affected her singing career. City AM described the documentary as 'a refreshingly intimate look at a constant figure in the world of pop.' The London Evening Standard also liked it, saying: 'A raw, heartbreaking and deeply moving window into the reclusive life of a once-in-a-generation talent cut down in its prime.'Where to watch it: I Am: Celine Dion is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video(Picture: Amazon MGM Studios)

Back to the 90s now for this stunning, underrated gem from director Richard Linklater, starring Ethan Hawke and Julie Delpy as students travelling round Europe, whose paths cross while he is en route to Vienna ahead of returning to the US the next morning. The two strangers quickly form a strong connection, and spend the night wandering the city before his flight leaves - and facing some awkward choices, even though they have only known each other a matter of hours. It's charming, and visually arresting, and we can't guarantee you won't be a bit misty-eyed by the time the credits roll. The critics, meanwhile, praised it for its realism, with Roger Ebert saying in the Chicago Sun-Times: 'Before Sunrise is so much like real life that I found myself remembering real conversations I had experienced with more or less the same words.'Where to watch it: Before Sunrise is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+ and Google Play(Picture: Moviestore/REX/Shutterstock)

Is there anybody left in the world who hasn't seen Singin' In The Rain, given how often it seems to pop up on TV on Christmas and bank holidays? If you are one of those handful of folk then it's about time you did check it out, because even if you hate musicals you can't help but appreciate the smart, witty script and brilliant performances from the likes of Gene Kelly and Debbie Reynolds. Set in the early days of Hollywood, it follows silent movie stars Don Lockwood (Kelly) and Lina Lamont (Jean Hagen) and the comical events which unfold when the two finally have to reveal their voices on film in their first talking picture. Reynolds, meanwhile, sparkles as the chorus girl who gets an unexpected shot at stardom. And then of course there's that title track, the one we've all sung when stepping out the door into a downpour. Don't believe us? Then listen to Time Out, who said quite simply: 'If you've never seen it and don't, you're bonkers.' Where to watch it: Singin' In The Rain is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+ and Google Play(Picture: MGM)

We haven't seen a lot of horror on this list so far, with the genre very rarely proving perfect enough for the critics to scream in unison. However this 2017 zombie comedy from Japan has proven popular enough to get that all-important 100%. The movie follows a group of filmmakers and actors who gather to make a zombie film for live TV which has to be shot in a single take, with the first part of the movie showing us the film within the film, before it leaps back in time to show us the origins of the film before it became a film. Are you keeping up? Never mind. Just watch it and see the mayhem, the comedy and the inevitable twists unfold before your eyes. As Collider put in their review: 'One Cut of the Dead is an absolute blast, and you should know as little about the plot as possible before seeing the film'. So forget everything you just read.Where to watch it: One Cut Of The Dead is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video(Picture: Arrow)

Moving on to another Netflix documentary which kept the critics gripped, Athlete A tells the story of the gymnasts who survived USA Gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar's abuse and the reporters from the Indianapolis Star who exposed the toxic culture of USAG. Given the harrowing stories that emerge from those involved, this isn't easy viewing at all - but it's a gripping story which needed to be told. Cosmopolitan said of the film: 'The documentary is a powerful reminder of how organizations can perpetuate abuse', while Uproxx said it 'makes you rethink everything you thought about the Olympic dream'.Where to watch it: Athlete A is available to watch on Netflix(Picture: Courtesy of Netflix)

There are some movies you definitely shouldn't watch on an empty stomach, and 1985's Japanese comedy Tampopo is one of those - although even if you do eat before watching it it'll probably make you hungry anyway. The film follows a truck driver and his sidekick who stop at a roadside noodle shop and get involved in the owner's bid to create the best noodles in the world. There's all sorts of other weirdness going on in this one, involving comic asides and a surprising level of sensuality - but ultimately it's the food which takes centre stage. 'One of its particular charms is that it celebrates as much as satirizes,' said the Philadelphia Inquirer. 'No movie gourmet with exotic tastes should miss it'.Where to watch it: Tampopo is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video(Picture: Everett/REX/Shutterstock)

This French drama, originally set to screen at the 2020 Cannes Film Festival before it was cancelled in the wake of the pandemic, tells the story of Lyz, a 15-year-old ski prodigy who wins a place at a prestigious ski school. However her coach's determination to make her a star extends beyond her prowess on the slopes, as his interest in her turns predatory. As well as being gripping, compelling viewing, the timely #metoo theme struck a chord with critics. CineVue said: 'Directed with both sensitivity and brio, this gripping and haunting drama gets to the heart of the power that abusers hold over their victims'.Where to watch it: Slalom is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+ and Google Play(Picture: jour2fete)

Paul Newman gave some pretty legendary performances throughout his career, from Butch Cassidy and The Sundance Kid and The Sting through to later roles in The Color Of Money and Nobody's Fool - but this remains one of his definitive screen appearances. Cool Hand Luke sees Newman as an inmate in a Florida prison camp who refuses to submit to the system, escaping every time he is captured - until the  prison staff come up with a plan to beat him at his own game. The iconic egg-eating scene is the one everybody remembers but there's a lot more to enjoy here, with Total Film saying: 'It's easy to forget just how fine Cool Hand Luke is' and The Hollywood Reporter adding: 'Luke succeeds as a highly humorous and deeply dramatic study of the immolation of human spirit in capitivity, and as an allegory'.Where to watch it: Cool Hand Luke is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+ and Google Play(Picture: Warner Bros/Kobal/REX/Shutterstock)

Back to Netflix now, and this 2020 documentary which tells the story of Terry Donahue, a former player in the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League (the team which inspired the 1992 movie A League Of Their Own) and her relationship with partner Pat Henschel. The pair met in 1947 and went on to run a successful interior decorating business together in the 1980s - but they kept their love a secret from their families for almost seven decades. The film not only tells their story but also examines the challenges the couple faced with coming out in later life. It's an amazing, emotional story with the critics quick to voice their approval. 'A Secret Love is guaranteed to pull at your heartstrings,' said Associated Press, while The Guardian added: '"There's no crying in baseball!" Tom Hanks's grumpy coach said in A League of Their Own, but I was bawling my eyes out watching this film.'Where to watch it: A Secret Love is available to watch on Netflix(Picture: Netflix)

Yet another full-on classic finds its way on to the list, and this time it's the gripping courtroom drama about the murder trial of a teenage boy, and the jurors who must deliberate his fate. While shut in a room together, one of their number (Henry Fonda) starts to cast doubt on certain elements of the case - and differences and disagreements start to fly among the jurors, leading them to question their own morals and values. 'The film leaves a tremendous impact,' Variety said in their review, and they're not wrong about that.Where to watch it: 12 Angry Men is available to watch on ITVX, NOW TV and Google Play(Picture: Moviestore/REX/Shutterstock)

Actor Christopher Reeve found fame in the late 70s and 80s playing Superman on screen before a tragic horse-riding accident in 1995 left him paralysed from the neck down until his death, aged 52, in 2004. This documentary - already attracting stellar reviews even though it's not released in the UK until November - takes a look at his life from movie star who set the benchmark for the modern-day cinematic universes, through to activist and campaigner to find a cure for spinal cord injuries. The Hollywood Reporter called the film 'a powerful story of human endurance', while IndieWire added: 'As much as it’s a movie about one man’s struggle, it’s a family drama too, and the way his paralysis shifts their dynamic over the years is enrapturing to watch'.Where to watch it: Super/Man: The Christopher Reeve Story is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video, and is also showing in selected cinemas(Picture: Katie Chew)

You might have seen this one before since it previously aired as part of the BBC's Storyville series, but it's well worth your time if you haven't. The film, which won the 2007 Oscar for best documentary feature, centres on the case of an Afghan taxi driver who died five days after he had been taken for questioning at Bagram Force Air Base. With the case remaining unsolved, it goes on to examine the wider claims of torture occurring at bases such as Guantanamo Bay, following the events of 9/11. Reviews were as glowing as you might expect, with Empire saying: 'An unflinching documentary that exposes one of the darkest chapters in American history.'Where to watch it: Taxi To The Dark Side is available to watch on Apple TV+(Picture: Jigsaw Prods/Kobal/REX/Shutterstock)

Ealing Studios churned out many a classic comedy at the height of its powers in the 40s and 50s but few were quite as brilliant as this darkly comic effort. Sir Alex Guinness takes the lead as all eight members of the aristocratic Gascoyne clan - with one of them, Louis, attempting to get his hands on the family dukedom by murdering all of those ahead of him in the succession line. Regarded as one of the best British films of all time, it's worth seeing for Guinness' performance(s) alone. The Telegraph said of it: 'A high comedy that is enlivened with cynicism, loaded with dramatic irony and shot through with a suspicion of social satire.' Which pretty much sums it up.Where to watch it: Kind Hearts and Coronets is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+ and Google Play(Picture: Allstar/EALING STUDIOSSTUDIOCANAL)

Carrie Fisher and Debbie Reynolds tragically died within two days of each other in December 2016 - and this documentary marks Reynolds' final screen appearance, with the HBO-produced movie airing just weeks after they had both passed away. Despite the tragic circumstances which preceeded it, it's a wonderful tribute to the mother/daughter movie legends - best known for their roles in Star Wars and Singin' In The Rain, respectively - with their relationship being examined via interviews, photos, vintage home movies and other footage. Reviews were as sparkling as you might expect, with iNews saying: 'Beneath the glitz and glamour, Bright Lights told a story of family wounds that run deep - a tale we mere mortals can relate to as well'.Where to watch it: Bright Lights: Starring Carrie Fisher and Debbie Reynolds is available to watch on Amazon Prime Video and Google Play (Picture: HBO)

Finally, another British movie, one which caused quite a stir when it was released in 2019, picking up awards at film festivals across the world. Set in Cornwall, and filmed using a hand-cranked camera, the movie sees Modern-day Cornish fisherman Martin (Edward Rowe) struggling to buy a boat while coping with family rivalry and the influx of tourists to his small harbour village. Tensions rise further over the summer as a family from out of town use a cottage they rented from Martin and his brother Steven as a seasonal holiday home - and things ultimately reach boiling point, with tragic consequences. Mark Kermode summed this one up in the Observer, saying: 'It's a genuine modern masterpiece, which establishes (director) Mark Jenkin as one of the most arresting and intriguing British film-makers of his generation'.Where to watch it: Bait is available to watch on ITVX, Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+ and Google Play(Picture: Early Day Films)
How many of these films have you seen? Share your views in the comments!
